name: JK Creative Wood & Gifts
old_description: Subscribe to our mailing list for insider news, product launches, and more.
about:
JK Creative Wood & Gifts operates from Kalona, Iowa, where it maintains a physical storefront and an online shop built on Shopify. The company does not disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders' names on its website. Its branding references "Representing Six Generations" in connection with Amish furniture traditions, though it is unclear whether this refers to the business itself or its supply partners.

The retailer curates and sells handmade wooden gifts, jewelry, and kitchen and dining accessories. Its product lineup includes customizable wooden letter trains, mini pocket teleidoscopes, wooden pocket mirrors, and small secret boxes priced from $6 to $23. The merchandise is described as "Heirloom Amish Furniture" and "Handmade by Artists Across America," indicating that JK Creative Wood & Gifts sources finished goods from independent artisans and Amish workshops rather than manufacturing in house.

The store serves consumer markets seeking gift items, home decor, and novelty wooden products. There is no indication of business-to-business sales, wholesale programs, or industrial supply relationships in the available content.

The company positions its differentiation on the heritage of Amish craftsmanship and the breadth of its artisan network, summarizing its offering as "Handmade by Artists Across America." No explicit mission statement or founding rationale is provided.

about:
JSB Car Parts operates from Dover, Delaware, where it runs an online store serving automotive enthusiasts and professionals across the United States. The company was established to provide a curated selection of car parts and accessories, though the exact founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The retailer stocks a broad range of automotive products, including interior accessories, safety harnesses, racing seats, vehicle lifts, jacks, motor oils, and performance fluids. Brands carried include TUFFIOM, VEVOR, Mophorn, Castrol, Royal Purple, Sparco, OMP, and Thrustmaster. The company does not manufacture its own parts; instead, it sources and resells components for passenger vehicles, racing, and sim-racing applications.

Customers include DIY enthusiasts, professional mechanics, and competitive drivers seeking replacement parts, safety gear, and performance upgrades. The product catalog spans categories such as automotive protective gear, racing safety equipment, lubricants, and simulation hardware, reflecting a focus on both street and track use.

According to its mission statement, JSB Car Parts aims to empower every vehicle owner with quality parts while fostering a community built on trust, excellence, and a passion for automotive culture. The company emphasizes expert support and a curated shopping experience as key differentiators.

name: JSL Foods Inc, Texas
old_description: Ask us about our ability to deliver 14 points of customization to support your entrée, side, or brand!
about:
JSL Foods Inc operates from Humble, Texas. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company provides custom food manufacturing services, offering what it describes as 14 points of customization for entrées, sides, and private-label brands. Its production processes include ingredient selection, recipe creation, testing, and qualification. The facility operates under a Safe Quality Food (SQF) program and follows Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).

JSL Foods serves food brands and manufacturers seeking custom entrée and side products. Its client base includes companies requiring USDA, Organic, and Kosher certified production.

The company emphasizes its quality and safety programs as differentiators, citing high 90s audit scores from consumers and third-party regulators. It maintains certifications including USDA, Organic, Kosher, NSF, and OSHA compliance, and states a commitment to continuous improvement of its protocols.

name: JT AUTO
old_description: Thank you so much for considering SIAS! Unfortunately, due to a labor shortage, SIAS has temporarily decided to stop taking on new customers.
about:
Specialized Import Auto Service (SIAS) has operated from Anchorage, Alaska since 1988. The family-owned shop was founded by James Trueblood and occupies a facility on West Dimond Boulevard, serving the Anchorage and Eagle River communities.

The shop provides repair and maintenance for imported cars, trucks, and SUVs. Its team of ASE Certified Master Technicians uses state-of-the-art diagnostic equipment to service makes including Toyota, Honda, Subaru, Nissan, Hyundai, Mercedes, Audi, BMW, Lexus, and Volkswagen. Services range from routine oil changes and tire inflation to complex transmission, engine, and drivetrain work, always using manufacturer-recommended fluids specified for each vehicle.

Customers are primarily individual vehicle owners in the Anchorage and Eagle River area who drive imported vehicles. The shop handles all import makes and models, from daily commuters to off-road SUVs, and also performs factory warranty service as an alternative to dealership visits.

Trueblood started the business to offer honest, reliable import auto repair at more affordable prices than dealerships, emphasizing quality parts and taking the extra time to do jobs right the first time. A labor shortage in early 2023 led the company to temporarily stop accepting new customers to maintain service levels for its existing base.

name: Jack Lederman Co Inc
old_description: Some of our most unique projects so far have been in using custom fabrication to meet the needs of our customers.
about:
Jack Lederman Co. Inc. operates from Kearney, Nebraska, where it has served the central Nebraska area for over 70 years. The company is a small business; no founding year or founder names are disclosed in public sources.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication, welding (TIG, MIG, arc, spot, stick), and machining services. It maintains a shear, brake, press, and tube bender, and runs portable welding equipment for on‑site and field work. Projects range from light and heavy off‑ and on‑highway equipment repair and fabrication to metal sign fabrication, antique equipment repair or replication, custom fencing, gates, railings, steel tanks, boxes, livestock panels, and patio furniture repair. The company also stocks what it describes as the most complete steel inventory in central Nebraska, working with new and used steel, aluminum, and other materials.

Customers span agriculture and ranching, commercial and residential construction, and industrial equipment operators. The firm also subcontracts welding services to other businesses in the region.

Lederman emphasizes its diverse background, local partnerships, mobile welding capability, and free estimates as differentiators.

name: Jackson Furniture / Catnapper
old_description: Our TN plants will resume business operations at 9AM Wed the 17th
about:
Jackson Furniture Industries, operating under the Catnapper brand, is headquartered in Cleveland, Tennessee. The company was founded in the United States and remains focused on domestic manufacturing, though a specific founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed. It operates as a privately held enterprise with no stated veteran, woman, or family ownership designation.

The company produces residential furniture including reclining sofas, sectionals, and seating sets across 10 factories. Its manufacturing processes feature computer-cut wood parts reinforced with extra glue and stapling, steel springs made from 12-gauge heat-tempered steel in the back and 8-gauge steel in the seat, an exclusive Steel Tech framing system with steel rails and stretchers, Comfort Gel layers for cooler seating and reduced motion transfer, and comfort coil seat cushions backed by a five-year warranty. The operation employs over 1,500 dedicated employees and vendors.

Jackson Furniture serves the residential furniture market primarily through a network of retail partners. Its products are sold to consumers via brick-and-mortar retailers, with the company providing a "Find A Retailer" tool on its website. No specific commercial or institutional customers are named.

The company emphasizes its American-made heritage and community investment. Over the past five years, it has contributed more than $1.5 million to organizations including Habitat for Humanity, the American Heart Association, the Anti-Defamation League, the United Way, and the Boy Scouts of America. This philanthropic focus, combined with a domestic production footprint, is presented as a core differentiator.

name: Janco Electronics Inc.
old_description: Janco Electronics is a People-First Contract Assembly Company
about:
Janco Electronics Inc. operates from Rollinsford, New Hampshire. The business traces its roots to 1958 when brothers Lewis, George, and Paul Janetos founded the Janco Company, initially introducing plastic materials for Green Bay Packers shoulder pads. In 1966 the company expanded into electronics manufacturing, and in 1985 Lewis E. Janetos incorporated Janco Electronics as a separate entity. The founder led the company until 2001, when his son Rollins Janetos assumed the presidency, keeping the firm family-owned.

The company provides full-service electronics contract manufacturing and assembly. Core processes include surface‑mount pick‑and‑place, through‑hole technology, fine‑pitch BGA placement and rework, electro‑mechanical system integration, flex‑circuit assembly, conformal coating, and a range of test services such as flying‑probe, in‑circuit, functional, RF/microwave, and 2D X‑ray with 3D capability. Additional offerings cover new‑product introduction (NPI), design‑for‑manufacturability (DFM), cable‑assembly prototyping, supply‑chain management, turnkey assembly, just‑in‑time (JIT) manufacturing, and counterfeit‑component mitigation. A modern facility houses the equipment and certified technicians; headcount is not publicly disclosed. Production spans prototype through high‑volume runs.

Janco serves customers in defense, medical (including medical‑device manufacturing), commercial, industrial, automotive, aerospace, and telecommunications/RF sectors. Its client base consists primarily of original‑equipment manufacturers requiring high‑reliability electronic assemblies and box‑build integration.

The company states that its founding philosophy — articulated by Lewis E. Janetos — centers on valuing people as the primary resource for continuous improvement and innovation. Quality is underscored by ISO 13485:2016 certification, adherence to IPC‑A‑610 and J‑STD‑001 standards, and lean‑manufacturing practices.

name: Jarvis Products Corporation
old_description: Learn more about the commitment we make to our people, our products, and our planet.
about:
Jarvis Products Corporation is headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. The company develops automated machinery and tooling for meat, poultry, and fish processing plants. No founding year or ownership details are disclosed in public sources.

Its product line includes the JLR-900 pork splitting robot, described as the fastest of its kind, along with a range of power tools and automated modules for slaughter and fabrication lines. Jarvis also designs and manufactures original spare parts and consumables packages, which it supplies globally. The company operates a worldwide service network with field-trained teams in more than 23 countries, offering scheduled maintenance, 24/7 in-plant specialist support, emergency repairs, blade reconditioning and leasing, and free operator training on purchased equipment. An in-house research and development group partners with customers to create tailored automation solutions.

Customers span industrial meat and poultry processors, seafood operations, and smaller family-run farms and delis. The firm serves the broader food processing industry, focusing on automation that addresses labor shortages and throughput demands in the supply chain.

Jarvis states that its focus on automation reflects a mission to align with challenges and opportunities in the food system, guided by a commitment to its people, products, and the planet. The company emphasizes innovation for a healthier world and stewardship across its operations.
